description: Two Atlantic revolutions, three decades apart in spark but tightly linked in ideas, money, and people.

events.title: Stamp Act Congress
events.desc: Delegates from nine colonies met in New York to organize resistance to Britain's new direct tax on printed materials.

events.title: Boston Massacre
events.desc: British soldiers fired on a crowd of colonists in Boston, hardening colonial opposition to British rule.

events.title: Boston Tea Party
events.desc: Colonists boarded British ships and destroyed tea shipments to protest taxation without representation.

events.title: First Continental Congress
events.desc: Delegates from twelve colonies convened in Philadelphia to coordinate a unified response to British policy.

events.title: Lexington and Concord
events.desc: The first armed clashes of the American Revolutionary War broke out in Massachusetts.

events.title: Declaration of Independence
events.desc: The Second Continental Congress declared the thirteen colonies free of British rule, drawing heavily on Enlightenment ideas that would soon echo in France.

events.title: Battle of Trenton
events.desc: Washington's surprise crossing of the Delaware and attack on Trenton revived a flagging Continental Army.

events.title: Battle of Saratoga
events.desc: An American victory in New York proved a turning point, persuading France to openly back the rebellion.

events.title: Franco-American Alliance
events.desc: France formally allied with the United States, sending fleets, troops, and money that helped tip the war.

events.title: Siege of Yorktown
events.desc: A combined American and French force compelled the surrender of a major British army in Virginia, effectively ending the war.

events.title: Treaty of Paris
events.desc: Britain formally recognized American independence; France's war spending left its own treasury deeply strained.

events.title: US Constitutional Convention
events.desc: Delegates in Philadelphia drafted a new framework of federal government to replace the weak Articles of Confederation.

events.title: Estates-General convenes
events.desc: Facing bankruptcy after aiding America, Louis XVI summoned France's Estates-General for the first time in over a century.

events.title: Storming of the Bastille
events.desc: Parisians attacked the fortress-prison, a flashpoint that ignited the French Revolution.

events.title: Declaration of the Rights of Man
events.desc: The National Assembly adopted a founding statement of individual liberty and civic equality.

events.title: Women's March on Versailles
events.desc: Parisian market women marched on the royal palace demanding bread, forcing the king back to Paris.

events.title: Flight to Varennes
events.desc: Louis XVI's attempt to flee France in disguise was intercepted, shattering public trust in the monarchy.

events.title: France declares war on Austria
events.desc: The Revolutionary government went to war with Austria and Prussia, beginning decades of European conflict.

events.title: French Republic proclaimed
events.desc: The National Convention abolished the monarchy and declared France a republic.

events.title: Execution of Louis XVI
events.desc: The former king was executed by guillotine, radicalizing the revolution and alarming monarchies across Europe.

events.title: Reign of Terror begins
events.desc: The Committee of Public Safety launched a campaign of mass arrests and executions against perceived enemies of the revolution.

events.title: Fall of Robespierre
events.desc: Robespierre was arrested and executed, ending the Terror and opening a more moderate phase of the revolution.

events.title: The Directory established
events.desc: A five-member executive body took power in France, governing through a period of instability and corruption.

events.title: Napoleon's coup of 18 Brumaire
events.desc: Napoleon Bonaparte seized power in France, ending the Revolution's turbulent decade and beginning his rise.
